metadata.title: The Weighted Majority Algorithm
metadata.authors: Nick Littlestone and Manfred K. Warmuth
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: On-line prediction protocol
nodes.statement: Learning proceeds in a sequence of trials. In each trial the algorithm receives an instance from a fixed domain, produces a binary prediction, then receives a binary label; a mistake occurs if prediction and label disagree.

nodes.name: Master algorithm and pool
nodes.statement: A master algorithm receives the predictions of a pool $A$ of prediction algorithms and forms its own prediction; the same instance is fed to all pool members and the label is passed back to the entire pool.

nodes.name: Anomaly count
nodes.statement: The number of anomalies of a sequence of trials with respect to a target function $f$ is the number of trials whose label differs from $f$'s value at the instance; with respect to a class $F$, it is the minimum over $f \in F$.

nodes.name: Total weight notation $w_{init}, w_{fin}, q_0, q_1$
nodes.statement: Each pool member has a positive weight; $w_{init}$ is the total initial weight, $w_{fin}$ is the total final weight; in a trial $q_0$ (resp. $q_1$) is the total weight of pool members predicting $0$ (resp. $1$).

nodes.name: Absolute loss
nodes.statement: If an algorithm predicts $x$ in a trial with label $\lambda$, its loss in that trial is $|x - \lambda|$; total loss $m_i = \sum_{j=1}^{t} |x_i^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|$ for pool member $i$ and $m = \sum_{j=1}^{t} |\hat{\lambda}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|$ for the master.

nodes.name: Weighted average prediction $\hat{\nu}^{(j)}$
Weak / strong independence conditions
nodes.statement: Weak: $E(\hat{\lambda}^{(j)} \mid (x^{(1)},\lambda^{(1)}),\ldots,(x^{(j)},\lambda^{(j)})) = \hat{\nu}^{(j)}$ (a.s.). Strong: same with conditioning extended to all $(x^{(i)},\lambda^{(i)})_{i=1}^t$ and past predictions $\hat{\lambda}^{(1)},\ldots,\hat{\lambda}^{(j-1)}$.

nodes.name: Shattered function class
nodes.statement: A set $\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\}$ of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions on $X$ is shattered by $X$ if $(\varphi_1(x),\ldots,\varphi_n(x))$ ranges over all of $\{0,1\}^n$ as $x$ ranges over $X$ (dual to VC shattering).

nodes.name: Mistake tree and $\mathrm{opt}(F,\nu)$
nodes.statement: A mistake tree for $F$ over $X$ is a binary tree whose nodes are non-empty subsets of $F$ (root $= F$), with internal nodes labeled by $x \in X$ and children given by the consistent / inconsistent function subsets at $x$. $\mathrm{opt}(F,\nu)$ is the worst-case mistake count of the best deterministic algorithm on sequences with $\le \nu$ anomalies; $\mathrm{opt}_{RAND}$ is the analogous expected mistake count.

nodes.name: Weighted Majority Algorithm (WM)
nodes.statement: Maintain a positive weight per pool member; predict the side with larger total weight $q_0$ vs $q_1$; on a mistake, multiply by $\beta \in [0,1)$ the weight of every pool member whose prediction disagreed with the label.
output: A binary prediction in $\{0,1\}$ at each trial

nodes.name: Weighted Majority with Lower threshold (WML)
nodes.statement: Variant of WM with two parameters $\beta \in [0,1), \gamma \in [0,1/2)$: identical to WM except that an update is skipped if the weight before update is smaller than $\frac{\gamma}{|A|}$ times the total weight; this prevents weights from collapsing and supports a shifting target.
output: Updated weights, none ever falling below the threshold

nodes.name: Weighted Majority for Infinite pools (WMI2)
nodes.statement: Variant of WM for a countably infinite pool that maintains an active subpool of indices $1..l$ which grows whenever the inequality $\hat{W}(l+1) \le \frac{u^{m+1}}{(1-\beta)(m+1)(m+2)} \hat{W}(1)$ fails ($u = (1+\beta)/2$, $m$ = mistakes so far); predicts only when the weight gap exceeds the inactive-mass slack to allow finite-precision computation.
input: Countably infinite pool $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ with computable simulation
Computable weight function $W$ and a tail bound $\hat{W}(i) \ge \sum_{j \ge i} W(j)$ with $\hat{W}(i) \to 0$

nodes.name: Generalized Weighted Majority (WMG)
nodes.statement: Pool predictions $x_i^{(j)} \in [0,1]$, master prediction binary; predict $1$ if $\hat{\nu}^{(j)} > 1/2$, else $0$ (either at $1/2$). Update each weight by $w_i^{(j+1)} = F\, w_i^{(j)}$ with $F$ satisfying $\beta^{|x_i^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|} \le F \le 1 - (1-\beta)|x_i^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|$.

nodes.name: Continuous Weighted Majority (WMC)
nodes.statement: Pool predictions, master prediction, and labels all in $[0,1]$; master predicts $\hat{\lambda}^{(j)} = \hat{\nu}^{(j)}$ (the weighted average); update step satisfies the same inequality as WMG and is applied at every trial.

nodes.name: Randomized Weighted Majority (WMR)
nodes.statement: Pool predictions in $[0,1]$, labels binary; master predicts $1$ with probability $\hat{\nu}^{(j)}$ and updates weights every trial by the same multiplicative rule as WMG/WMC.
output: Random binary prediction in $\{0,1\}$ at each trial

nodes.name: Halving Algorithm
nodes.statement: Master algorithm that predicts according to the majority vote of all pool functions consistent with the trials seen so far; equivalent to WM with $\beta = 0$ and equal initial weights on a pool of functions.
nodes.origin_citation: Angluin 1988; Barzdin & Freivalds 1972; named in Littlestone 1988

nodes.name: Mistake bound for WM (Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be any sequence of instances and binary labels and let $m$ be the number of mistakes of WM on $S$. Then $m \le \frac{\log(w_{init}/w_{fin})}{\log \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$.
assumptions: WM applied to a pool $A$ with positive initial weights

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: Show that on a mistake the total weight after the trial is at most $\frac{1+\beta}{2}$ times the total before; combine $w_{init} u^m \ge w_{fin}$ with $u = (1+\beta)/2$ to invert and get the bound.

nodes.name: Per-trial weight contraction on a mistake
nodes.statement: WLOG learner predicts $0$ so $q_0 \ge q_1$; total after the update is $\beta q_0 + q_1 \le q_0 + q_1 + \frac{\beta - 1}{2}(q_0 - q_1) = \frac{1+\beta}{2}(q_0 + q_1)$.

nodes.name: Iterate and invert
nodes.statement: Iterating over the $m$ mistakes gives $w_{fin} \ge w_{init} u^m$ with $u = (1+\beta)/2$; inverting yields $m \le \log(w_{init}/w_{fin}) / \log(1/u)$.

nodes.name: Best-expert bound for WM (Corollary 2.1)
nodes.statement: If the $i$-th algorithm of pool $A$ ($|A|=n$) makes $m_i$ mistakes on $S$, then WM with equal initial weights makes at most $\frac{\log n + m_i \log(1/\beta)}{\log \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$ mistakes.

nodes.name: Subpool best-case bound (Corollary 2.2)
nodes.statement: If a subpool of size $k$ within $A$ ($|A|=n$) each makes at most $m$ mistakes, WM with equal initial weights makes at most $\frac{\log(n/k) + m \log(1/\beta)}{\log \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$ mistakes.
assumptions: Subpool of $k$ algorithms each with mistake count $\le m$

nodes.name: Subpool aggregate-mistake bound (Corollary 2.3)
nodes.statement: If a subpool of size $k$ in $A$ has total mistake count at most $\hat{m}$ on $S$, then WM with equal initial weights makes at most $\frac{\log(n/k) + (\hat{m}/k) \log(1/\beta)}{\log \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$ mistakes.
assumptions: Subpool of $k$ algorithms with total mistakes $\le \hat{m}$

nodes.name: WML one-segment bound (Lemma 3.1)
nodes.statement: If each initial weight is at least $\gamma/n$ times the total initial weight, then WML on pool $A$ ($|A|=n$) makes at most $\frac{\log(n/\gamma) + m_0 \log(1/\beta)}{\log(1/u)}$ mistakes on $S$, where $u = \frac{1+\beta}{2} + (1-\beta)\gamma$ and $m_0$ is the minimum pool-member mistake count.
assumptions: Initial weights $\ge \gamma/n$ of total initial weight
conclusions: Final weights also satisfy the threshold condition

nodes.name: WML shifting-target bound (Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be partitioned into $k$ subsequences $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ with lengths $l_i$, and let $m_i$ be the minimum pool-member mistakes on $S_i$. Then WML makes at most $\sum_{i=1}^k \min\bigl(l_i,\ \tfrac{\log(n/\gamma) + m_i \log(1/\beta)}{\log(1/u)}\bigr)$ mistakes, with $u = \tfrac{1+\beta}{2} + (1-\beta)\gamma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3.1 to each subsequence $S_i$, using the fact that the threshold condition on weights is preserved across segments.

nodes.name: WMI2 properties (Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: For WMI2 on a countably infinite pool with the $i$-th algorithm making $\le m_i$ mistakes: (1) active-pool size is the minimum $l$ with $\hat{W}(l+1) \le \frac{u^{m+1}}{(1-\beta)(m+1)(m+2)} \hat{W}(1)$; (2) $\sum_{i \ge 1} \omega_i \le (2 - \frac{1}{m+1}) u^m \hat{W}(1)$; (3) total mistakes $\le \inf_{i \ge 1} \frac{\log(\hat{W}(1)/W(i)) + m_i \log(1/\beta) + \log 2}{\log(1/u)}$ for $\beta>0$, and $\le 1 + \log_2(\hat{W}(1)/W(i))$ if $\beta=0$ and some $m_i = 0$.
conclusions: Three numbered claims on active-pool size, weight-sum bound, and mistake bound (see statement)

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: Part 1 follows from the WMI2 construction; Part 2 by induction on $m$ using the chosen prediction inequality and inactive-mass tail bound; Part 3 by combining $\sum \omega_i \ge \beta^{m_i} W(i)$ with the upper bound from Part 2 and solving for $m$.

nodes.name: Active-pool size by construction
nodes.statement: Part 1 is immediate from the rule that increases $l$ until $\hat{W}(l+1) \le \frac{u^{m+1}}{(1-\beta)(m+1)(m+2)} \hat{W}(1)$.

nodes.name: Inductive weight-sum bound
nodes.statement: Inductively bound $\sum_i \omega_i$ after $m+1$ mistakes: split into $q_0, q_1$ and inactive tail $q^*$, use the prediction inequality $q_1 \ge q_0 + \frac{u^{m+1} \hat{W}(1)}{(1-\beta)(m+1)(m+2)}$ to derive $\sum \omega_i \le (2 - 1/(m+2)) u^{m+1} \hat{W}(1)$.

nodes.name: Solve for mistake bound
nodes.statement: Combine $\sum_i \omega_i \ge \beta^{m_i} W(i)$ with the upper bound from Part 2 and solve for $m$ to get the inf bound; specialise to $\beta=0$ for the consistent case.

nodes.name: WMI2 with weights $W(i) = 1/(i(i+1))$ (Corollary 4.1)
nodes.statement: With $W(i) = 1/(i(i+1))$ and $\hat{W}(i) = 1/i$: active pool size after $m$ mistakes is $\lceil (1-\beta)(m+1)(m+2)(2/(1+\beta))^{m+1} \rceil - 1$; mistake bound (for $\beta>0$) $\inf_{i \ge 1} \frac{\log_2(i(i+1)) + m_i \log_2(1/\beta) + 1}{\log_2 \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$.

nodes.name: WMI2 with $W(i) = 2^{-i}$ (Corollary 4.2)
nodes.statement: With $W(i) = 2^{-i}$, $\hat{W}(i) = 2^{-(i-1)}$: active-pool size grows as $\log_2(1/(1-\beta)) + \log_2((m+1)(m+2)) + (m+1)\log_2(1/u)$; total mistakes $\le \inf_{i \ge 1} \frac{i + m_i \log_2(1/\beta) + 1}{\log_2 \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$.

nodes.name: WMI2 with double-exponential weights (Corollary 4.3)
nodes.statement: With $W(i) = 2^{-2^{i-1}}$ and $\hat{W}(i) = 2 \cdot 2^{-2^{i-1}}$: active-pool size after $m$ mistakes is $\lceil \log_2[\log_2(1/(1-\beta)) + \log_2((m+1)(m+2)) + (m+1)\log_2(2/(1+\beta)) + 1] \rceil$; total mistakes $\le \inf_{i \ge 1} \frac{2^{i-1} + m_i \log_2(1/\beta) + 1}{\log_2 \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$.
conclusions: Active pool size grows logarithmically in $m$

nodes.name: $r$-of-$k$ threshold functions via WM and Winnow
nodes.statement: Apply WM (resp.\ WMI2) to the pool $\{A_{2^i}\}_{0 \le i \le \lceil \log_2 n \rceil}$ of Winnow tuned to powers of two; the master makes $O(kr \log n)$ mistakes on any sequence consistent with an $r$-of-$k$ threshold function on $\{0,1\}^n$, without knowing $r$.

nodes.name: Generalisation: parameter $q$ for class with parameters $(k,r)$
nodes.statement: Given an algorithm $A(q)$ with mistake bound $B(q,r) = q\, g(r)$ when $q \ge k$ and $g(r) \ge r_0$, applying WMI2 (with double-exponential weights) to $A(1), A(2), A(4), \ldots$ yields total mistakes $O(B(k, r))$ without knowing $k$.

nodes.name: Convexity inequality for $\beta^r$ (Lemma 5.1)
nodes.statement: For $\beta \ge 0$ and $0 \le r \le 1$, $\beta^r \le 1 + r(\beta - 1)$.

nodes.name: Log-weight contraction (Lemma 5.2)
nodes.statement: Under WMG/WMC update with $0 \le \beta < 1$ and $w_i^{(j+1)} \le w_i^{(j)}(1 - (1-\beta)|x_i^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|)$, either $w_{fin} = 0$ (in the $\beta=0$ degenerate case) or $\ln(w_{fin}/w_{init}) \le \sum_{j=1}^{t} \ln(1 - (1-\beta)|\hat{\nu}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|)$.

nodes.name: Linearised loss bound (Lemma 5.3)
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Lemma 5.2, $\sum_{j=1}^{t} |\hat{\nu}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}| \le \frac{\ln(w_{init}/w_{fin})}{1-\beta}$.

nodes.name: Mistake bound for WMG (Theorem 5.1)
nodes.statement: WMG (with $0 \le \beta < 1$) on a sequence $S$ with binary labels makes at most $m \le \frac{\log(w_{init}/w_{fin})}{\log \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$ mistakes.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: From Lemma 5.2 and the inequality $\log(1 - (1-\beta)|\hat{\nu}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|) \le m \log((1+\beta)/2)$ (only mistake-trials contribute meaningfully).

nodes.name: Best-expert WMG bound (Corollary 5.1)
nodes.statement: Equal initial weights, $\beta > 0$: WMG on pool $A$ ($|A|=n$) with pool-member total losses $m_i$ makes at most $\frac{\log n + m_i \log(1/\beta)}{\log \frac{2}{1+\beta}}$ mistakes, for any $1 \le i \le |A|$.

nodes.name: Loss bound for WMC (Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: For any sequence $S$ with labels in $[0,1]$, the total loss of WMC satisfies $m \le \frac{\ln(w_{init}/w_{fin})}{1-\beta}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2
nodes.statement: Immediate from Lemma 5.3 with $\hat{\lambda}^{(j)} = \hat{\nu}^{(j)}$, summing pointwise loss.

nodes.name: Best-expert WMC bound (Corollary 5.2)
nodes.statement: Equal initial weights: WMC has total loss at most $\frac{\ln n + m_i \ln(1/\beta)}{1-\beta}$ for any $1 \le i \le n$.

nodes.name: Expected mistake bound for WMR (Theorem 6.1)
nodes.statement: Under the weak independence condition, the expected number of mistakes of WMR on $S$ satisfies $E(m) \le \frac{E(\ln(w_{init}/w_{fin}))}{1-\beta}$ (deterministic instances/labels give $E(m) \le \ln(w_{init}/w_{fin})/(1-\beta)$).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1
nodes.statement: Weak independence yields $E(|\hat{\lambda}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|) = E(|\hat{\nu}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|)$; then sum over $j$ and apply Lemma 5.3.

nodes.name: Best-expert WMR bound (Corollary 6.1)
nodes.statement: Equal initial weights: $E(m_{\mathrm{WMR}}) \le \frac{\log n + E(m_i)\log(1/\beta)}{1-\beta}$ for any $1 \le i \le n$.

nodes.name: Chernoff bound for supermartingales (Theorem 6.2)
nodes.statement:
Let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_t$ be $[0,1]$-valued random variables and $c_1,\ldots,c_t$ be $\mathcal{G}$-measurable in $[0,1]$. Define $S_j = \sum_{i=1}^j (\xi_i - c_i)$, $S_0 = 0$, $
u =  rac{1}{t}\sum c_j$. If $((S_j, \mathcal{G}_j))$ is a supermartingale and $\eta$ is $\mathcal{G}$-measurable with $0 \le \eta \le 
u$, then on $\{0 < 
u < 1\}$, $P(S_t \ge \eta t \mid \mathcal{G}) \le e^{-\eta^2 t / (3
u)}$.

nodes.name: WMR concentration bound (Theorem 6.3)
nodes.statement: Under the strong independence condition, if $b$ is a high-prob upper bound on $E(m \mid (x^{(1)},\lambda^{(1)}),\ldots,(x^{(t)},\lambda^{(t)}))$ and $0 < a \le 1$, then $P(m > (1+a) b \mid (x^{(\cdot)},\lambda^{(\cdot)})) \le e^{-a^2 b / 3}$ a.s.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.3
nodes.statement: Construct $\xi_j = |\hat{\lambda}^{(j)} - \lambda^{(j)}|$ and a $\mathcal{G}$-measurable $c_j$ with $\sum c_j = b$; verify that the partial sums form a supermartingale under strong independence; apply Theorem 6.2 with $\eta = ab/t$, $\nu = b/t$.

nodes.name: Initial-weight mistake bound for WM on consistent pools (Theorem 7.1)
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n$ be a pool of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions and $M_1,\ldots,M_n \ge 0$ integers with $\sum_{i=1}^n 2^{-M_i} < 2$. WM with initial weights $w_j = 2^{-M_j}$ and $\beta = 0$ makes at most $M_i$ mistakes on any sequence consistent with $\varphi_i$.
conclusions: WM makes $\le M_i$ mistakes on the sequence

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.1
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 2.1: $\log_2 \sum_j 2^{-M_j} - \log_2 2^{-M_i} < 1 + M_i$; integrality of mistake count tightens to $\le M_i$.

nodes.name: Sum-decomposition lemma (Lemma 7.1)
nodes.statement: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_n > 0$ with $r_i / r_{i+1}$ integer. If $0 < s \le \sum_{i=1}^n r_i$ and $s/r_1$ is an integer, then there exists $m \le n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^m r_i = s$.

nodes.name: Power-of-two subset lemma (Lemma 7.2)
nodes.statement: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_j > 0$ with $\log_2 r_i$ integers and $\max_i r_i \le 2^l \le \sum_{i=1}^j r_i$. Then there exists $K \subset \{1,\ldots,j\}$ with $\sum_{i \in K} r_i = 2^l$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on shattered classes (Theorem 7.2)
nodes.statement: Let $\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\}$ be $\{0,1\}$-valued and shattered by its domain, $A$ any deterministic on-line learner, and $M_i$ the worst-case mistake count of $A$ on sequences consistent with $\varphi_i$ (assume all $M_i$ finite). Then $\sum_{i=1}^n 2^{-M_i} < 2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.2
nodes.statement: Adversary maintains weights $u_i = 2^{-M_i}$, picks instances using Lemma 7.2 so the consistent weight halves at each forced mistake; eventually some surviving $u_j$ exceeds $2^{k_1 - (t+1)}$ giving $\log_2 \sum 2^{-M_i} < 1$.

nodes.name: Adversary setup with weights $u_i$
nodes.statement: Initialise $u_i = 2^{-M_i}$; at iteration $r$ set $k_r = \lfloor \log_2 \sum_i u_i \rfloor$; if $\max u_i > 2^{k_r - 1}$ stop, else apply Lemma 7.2 to get $K$ with $\sum_{i \in K} u_i = 2^{k_r - 1}$.

nodes.name: Force a mistake using shattering
nodes.statement: Pick instance $x$ with $\varphi_i(x) = 0$ on $K$ and $\varphi_i(x) = 1$ off $K$ (possible by shattering); choose label opposite to learner's prediction; zero out inconsistent $u_i$.

nodes.name: Halving of $\sum u_i$ and termination
nodes.statement: After each iteration $\sum_i u_i$ shrinks by at least $2^{k_r - 1}$ but stays $\ge 2^{k_r - 1}$, so $k_r \ge k_{r-1} - 1$ and termination must occur.

nodes.name: Conclude $\sum 2^{-M_i} < 2$
nodes.statement: At termination $\max u_j > 2^{k_1 - (t+1)}$ with $t \le M_j$, giving $\log_2 \sum_i 2^{-M_i} < 1$ and hence $\sum_i 2^{-M_i} < 2$.

nodes.name: WM optimality on shattered classes (Corollary 7.1)
nodes.statement: If $\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\}$ is shattered by $X$ and a learner $A$ achieves mistake bound $M_i$ on $\varphi_i$ for all $i$, then WM with $w_j = 2^{-M_j}$ and $\beta = 0$ also achieves $\le M_i$ mistakes on $\varphi_i$.

nodes.name: Existence of universal mistake bound (Theorem 7.3)
nodes.statement: For computable $M_i$: (a) $\sum_{i \ge 1} 2^{-M_i}$ finite + computable to arbitrary precision $\Rightarrow$ (b) there exists $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and an algorithm $A$ such that $A$ makes $\le M_i + c$ mistakes on every sequence consistent with $\varphi_i$ for every domain and computably indexed pool $\Rightarrow$ (c) the same with the bound only required for $i \ge j$ for some $j > 0$ $\Rightarrow$ (d) $\sum_{i \ge 1} 2^{-M_i}$ is finite.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.3
nodes.statement: (a) $\Rightarrow$ (b): apply WMI2 with $\beta = 0$ and initial weights $2^{-M_i}$, take $c = \log_2 \hat{W}(1) + 1$. (c) $\Rightarrow$ (d): take $X = \{0,1\}^*$ and $\varphi_i(x) = $ ($i$-th bit of $x = 1$); the family $\varphi_j,\ldots,\varphi_n$ is shattered, so Theorem 7.2 forces $\sum_{i=j}^n 2^{-(M_i+c)} < 2$, hence convergence.

nodes.name: Barzdin-Freivalds bounds via WMI2 (Corollary 7.2)
nodes.statement: (a) For every domain $X$ and computably indexed total recursive $\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\ldots$ there exists an on-line algorithm $A$ with $M(A,\varphi_1)$ finite and $M(A,\varphi_i) = \log_2 i + \log_2 \log i + o(\log \log i)$ for $i > 1$. (b) There exist domain and class such that for every algorithm there are infinitely many $i$ with $M(A,\varphi_i) > \log_2 i + \log_2 \log i$.

nodes.name: Class size lower bound (Theorem 7.4)
nodes.statement: There exists a domain and computably indexed class such that for all $n \ge 1$ and all on-line learners $A$, some sequence consistent with a function in $\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\}$ forces at least $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ mistakes.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.4
nodes.statement: Use the same domain/class as in (c) $\Rightarrow$ (d) of Theorem 7.3; if $M$ is the max mistake bound, $n 2^{-M} < 2$ gives $M > \log_2 n - 1$, hence $M \ge \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ since $M$ is an integer.

nodes.name: Deterministic anomaly lower bound (Theorem 8.1)
nodes.statement:
For every target class $F$ and $
u \ge 0$ with $|F| > 1$: $\mathrm{opt}(F, 
u) \ge \mathrm{opt}(F, 0) + 2
u$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8.1
nodes.statement:
Adversary uses a complete $k$-mistake tree to force $k-1$ mistakes; then chooses an instance $x$ separated by two surviving functions $f_1, f_2$ and presents it $2
u+1$ times with adversarial labels, yielding $k + 2
u$ mistakes against $f_1$ (or $f_2$) with $\le 
u$ anomalies.

nodes.name: Randomized anomaly lower bound (Theorem 8.2)
nodes.statement:
For every target class $F$ and $
u \ge 0$ with $|F| > 1$: $\mathrm{opt}_{RAND}(F, 
u) \ge  rac{1}{2}\mathrm{opt}(F, 0) + 
u$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2
nodes.statement: Adapt the adversary of Theorem 8.1 by precomputing labels (independent of randomness): pick label $0$ iff the algorithm's probability of predicting $1$ exceeds $1/2$; this guarantees expected mistake $\ge 1/2$ at each forced trial.

nodes.name: Comparison: WMG vs WMC vs WMR vs Vovk
nodes.statement: WMG mistake bound is $\log(w_{init}/w_{fin}) / \log(2/(1+\beta))$; WMC and WMR (under independence) give $\ln(w_{init}/w_{fin})/(1-\beta)$, better by nearly a factor of two as $\beta \to 1$. Vovk's randomized rule attains $\ln(w_{init}/w_{fin}) / (2 \ln(2/(1+\beta)))$, exactly twice better than the deterministic WMG bound.

nodes.name: Anomaly application of WM and WMR (Section 8 discussion)
nodes.statement:
For WM the coefficient of $
u$ in the upper bound approaches $2$ as $ eta 	o 1$ (matching Theorem 8.1). For WMR, Corollary 6.1 gives $E(m) \le (\ln n + 
u \ln(1/ eta))/(1- eta)$, and Theorem 6.3 implies the coefficient of $
u$ can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ (matching Theorem 8.2).

nodes.name: Maass-style WMR satisfies strong independence (Theorem A.1)
nodes.statement: If WMR with $\beta = 0$, binary pool predictions, and Maass's lazy update (new random pool member chosen only after a mistake) is implemented with independent uniform $r^{(j)}$, then the strong independence condition holds.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem A.1
nodes.statement: By induction on the trial $j$, using Lemma A.1 to factor conditional expectations, show $P(\nu^{(j)} = k \mid (x^{(\cdot)}, \lambda^{(\cdot)}), \hat{\lambda}^{(1..j-1)}) = w_k^{(j)} / s^{(j)}$, which yields the strong independence condition.

nodes.name: Conditional expectation factorisation (Lemma A.1)
nodes.statement: If $\xi$ is a random variable with $E(|\xi|) < \infty$, $\eta$ is $\{0,1\}$-valued, $\mathcal{G}$ is a finite $\sigma$-algebra and $\mathcal{A} = \sigma(\mathcal{G}, \eta)$, then $E(\eta \xi \mid \mathcal{G}) = E(\eta \mid \mathcal{G})\, E(\xi \mid \mathcal{A})$ a.s.
